data.title: Google's New Gemini 4 Neon Joins Gemini 4 Argon at the Top of the DualEntry Accounting AI
data.description:
Google's New Gemini 4 Neon Joins Gemini 4 Argon at the Top of the DualEntry Accounting AI

Google's newly released Gemini 4 Neon got 91.1% of accounting tasks right on the DualEntry Accounting AI Benchmark, tying Google's Gemini 4 Argon for the highest score among 29 leading AI models tested.

Neon beat Argon on bank reconciliation (91.7% vs 75%) and on hard tasks (85.7% vs 82.1%). Argon was slightly more consistent (86.1% vs 85.1%) and cheaper per task.

Google's Gemini 4 Carbon is tied for third at 88.1% with Zhipu AI's GLM-5.3 Flash and SpaceXAI's Grok 4.7. That puts Google's models first, second and tied for third on the benchmark, the strongest showing by any provider.

Key findings:

  • Gemini 4 Neon scored 91.1% overall, tied for first of 29 with Gemini 4 Argon
  • Google's models are first, second and tied for third: Neon and Argon at 91.1%, then Gemini 4 Carbon at 88.1%, level with GLM-5.3 Flash and Grok 4.7
  • It leads Anthropic's best model, Claude Fable 5.1 (85.1%), by 6.0 points, and OpenAI's best, GPT-6.2 Sol (84.2%), by 6.9 points
  • It scored 100% on transaction classification and financial reporting, and 91.7% on accounts receivable and bank reconciliation
  • It scored 85.7% on hard tasks (24 of 28), ahead of Argon's 82.1%, and 97.2% on medium tasks (35 of 36)
  • Its consistency score was 85.1%, compared with 86.1% for Gemini 4 Argon
  • It costs $0.174 per task ($52.76 for a full benchmark run), about 50% more than Gemini 4 Argon ($0.115), and averages 24.3 seconds per task
  • On bank reconciliation it scored 91.7%, 16.7 points ahead of Argon

Gemini 4 Neon was not the strongest model in every category. Its weakest result came in month-end close at 66.7% (8 of 12), where Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 led at 91.7% and Argon scored 83.3%.

"Google now has two models tied at the top of our benchmark, and both get nine in ten accounting tasks right," said Benedict Dohmen, co-founder of DualEntry. "For finance teams the question is no longer whether AI can do the work, but whether it gets the same answer every time, and that is what separates the leaders."

The DualEntry Accounting AI Benchmark tests models on 101 synthetic accounting cases across eight areas: transaction classification, journal entries, accounts payable, accounts receivable, bank reconciliation, financial reporting, month-end close, and accounting knowledge.

Each model completes the full benchmark three times from an identical test company with the same tools and instructions. Answers are checked against reference answers written in advance using fixed scoring rules rather than an AI grader. No customer data is used.

Full results for all 29 models, including accuracy, consistency, cost, response time, and performance by accounting area, are available at dualentry.com/benchmark.

About DualEntry

DualEntry is the agentic, AI-native ERP for mid-market finance teams. It brings the general ledger, accounts payable and receivable, revenue recognition, multi-entity consolidation, and reporting into one platform, with AI agents that take on accounting work from data entry through close. Founded in 2024 and based in New York, DualEntry raised a $90 million Series A in 2025 from Lightspeed Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, and GV. Learn more at DualEntry.com.

Top Third-Party Logistics (3PL) Companies in the US for 2026

Top Third-Party Logistics (3PL) Companies in the US for 2026

PR Newswire

SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 19, 2026

An overview of providers serving DTC brands, multichannel retailers, specialized product categories and growing online businesses

SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- E-commerce businesses selling in the United States rely on fulfillment partners to store inventory, process orders, coordinate shipping and manage returns. The right provider depends on factors such as product type, order volume, sales channels and delivery expectations. This industry overview examines six companies with different fulfillment models and service strengths.

The companies were selected based on publicly available information about US warehousing, ecommerce order processing, technology integrations, shipping options, returns and specialized capabilities. They are presented alphabetically, not as a ranking of performance.

  1. Cart.com operates a nationwide fulfillment network and supports omnichannel order processing across direct-to-consumer, wholesale, retail and B2B channels. Its services include picking, packing, shipping, inventory visibility, kitting, bundling and Amazon FBA preparation.

  2. Fulfillment Service provides warehousing and order fulfillment from its facility in Traverse City, Michigan. It serves businesses from startups to established merchants, with no order minimums or long-term contracts and integrations with more than 40 shopping carts and marketplaces.

  3. Lansil Global combines US order fulfillment with China-based sourcing and manufacturing support. Its network includes a 98,221-square-foot Shenzhen facility, a 106,624-square-foot Nevada warehouse and a 32,069-square-foot Pennsylvania facility, totaling more than 236,000 square feet. The company reported shipping more than 20 million parcels worldwide by the end of 2025. Its experience spans industries such as Beauty & Cosmetics, Electronics, Jewelry & Accessories, Health & Wellness, Fashion & Apparel, and Home & Kitchen. Services include inventory management, order processing, kitting and bundling, Amazon FBA preparation and global distribution.

  4. Red Stag Fulfillment focuses on large, heavy and bulky products that require specialized storage, handling and shipping. Its services cover direct-to-consumer parcel orders, pallet shipments, retail distribution, Amazon fulfillment, returns and kitting.

  5. ShipBob supports DTC and B2B fulfillment through a distributed network of fulfillment centers in the US and other markets. Its services include inventory placement, picking, packing, shipping, returns and integrations with ecommerce platforms and sales channels.

  6. ShipMonk combines fulfillment operations with proprietary technology for inventory and order management. It serves DTC, B2B and retail businesses and offers kitting, customization, returns processing and integrations with ecommerce platforms and marketplaces.

What Should Businesses Consider When Choosing a 3PL Partner?

Businesses should compare warehouse locations with customer demand and review receiving, storage, pick-and-pack, shipping and returns fees. Platform integrations, inventory visibility, product dimensions, seasonal capacity, service-level commitments and support availability also affect whether a 3PL provider fits a brand's operating needs.

About Lansil Global

Founded in 2015, Lansil Global provides supply chain and ecommerce fulfillment services for brands selling through platforms such as Shopify and Amazon. Its services include China product sourcing, manufacturing support, quality control, China and US warehousing, order fulfillment, Amazon FBA preparation, custom packaging, returns processing and global freight. data.title: Is Social Security a Ponzi scheme? No, but fear is fueling such talk.
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

Wisconsin Republican Sen. Ron Johnson called Social Security a 'scam' and urged lawmakers to shut it down

Social Security is not a Ponzi scheme. A Ponzi scheme is born of fraud and relies on a constant stream of new unwitting investors.

Fear can lead us to do and say unexpected things.

It can push us toward panic selling, drive us to make wild assumptions about the world, and sometimes force us to take a hard look at our own finances. We are especially prone to these impulses when we are looking for something or someone to blame.

Wisconsin Republican Sen. Ron Johnson, the chairman of the Committee on the Budget, on Wednesday took aim at Social Security ahead of a hearing on the subject, calling it a scam. "It's grotesque and at this point, there really is no way to fix Social Security," he said. "It is a Ponzi scheme."

Social Security is not a Ponzi scheme. A Ponzi scheme is born of fraud and relies on a stream of new unwitting investors who pay the returns promised to earlier ones. Social Security is a pay-as-you-go program established by federal law, in which payroll taxes fund benefits.

He isn't the only one who's frustrated with Social Security. Experts attribute an expected shortfall in Social Security to demographic factors - older workers retiring, with some claiming benefits early out of fear that the funds will run out.

Social Security is a pay-as-you-go program established by federal law.

Unless Congress acts, the combined trust funds will run out in 2034, covering just 83% of benefits. A new AARP report said: "The share of gross domestic product subject to Social Security's payroll tax, the program's primary income source, has fallen steadily over the past four decades."

The Social Security taxable maximum is $184,500 for 2026 and $192,300 for 2027, meaning earnings above those limits are not subject to Social Security payroll taxes. In other words, a growing share of national income is excluded, contributing to the expected shortfall in funds.

Like Johnson, a Moneyist reader also used the "P" word. "The thought of living to 100 terrifies me more than dying. For me, the biggest fraud is telling people to wait until 70 to retire just to maximize their Social Security benefits - as if that's the only factor worth considering."

They continued: "I grew up in the 1980s, and the advice to never count on Social Security is sounding more and more like a warning than a prediction. I fear there will be a run on Social Security similar to the bank runs before the Great Depression. Long live the Ponzi!"

Don't miss: Is $1 million enough for a household to retire? The answer keeps changing.

Addressing the criticisms

The reader is essentially asking four questions: (1) Will fear trigger a Social Security crisis? (2) Is Social Security a Ponzi scheme? (3) Why sacrifice your 60s to get a bigger check at 70? And (4) Can you really count on Social Security?

(1) As for fear leading to a crisis: Probably not, so do not get carried away with 1930s-era prophecies of doom and gloom. A run on a bank involves a large number of people withdrawing their money and, if the bank cannot meet those withdrawals, even an otherwise solvent institution can fail.

I grew up in the 1980s too, and here's a fun fact about Generation X: The American Institute of Stress says we are apparently more stressed out than other generations. The main reason for that, researchers theorize, is that we are worried about falling short on our retirement goals.

(2) Social Security is a social-insurance program funded by workers and employers to provide support in retirement, prevent vulnerable people from falling into poverty and provide economic stability during downturns. It is at risk of a shortfall in funding, not annihilation.

Do not get carried away with 1930s prophecies of doom.

(3) You can claim Social Security at 62, but doing so reduces your monthly benefit by 30% compared with waiting until your full retirement age (FRA) of 67. Waiting until 70 increases your benefit by 8% for each year you delay beyond 67. That's 24% more in total.

If you are collecting Social Security and remain below FRA throughout 2026, you can earn up to $24,480 before benefits are withheld. Above that limit, $1 is withheld for every $2 you earn. At FRA, Social Security recalculates your benefit to account for withholdings.

Yes, some people do claim Social Security benefits early due to fears about the program's long-term viability. But the program values stability, security and peace of mind over recklessness, madcap investments and promises of riches.

(4) You can count on Social Security, which is not projected to disappear. Payroll taxes and other incoming revenue will keep funding benefits. Under current projections, though, that revenue would cover only 83% of scheduled benefits from the combined trust funds in 2034.

Don't miss: 'I still have horrible memories of the Bernie Madoff scandal': At 63, who can I trust with my $655K retirement fund?

Why we have Social Security

Social Security was created in 1935 in response to the Great Depression and was not intended to maximize investment returns. Today, it provides a social safety net against the financial hardships of retirement, disability and the loss of a family's breadwinner.

There are two separate funds: the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund and the Disability Insurance Trust Fund. Their reserves are invested in special-issue U.S. Treasury securities, backed by the full faith and credit of the federal government.

So what about this looming funding crisis? The Congressional Budget Office said earlier this year that the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund, which pays retirement and survivors benefits, is projected to run out of reserves in 2032.

The Bipartisan Policy Center, a Washington, D.C.-based think tank, said in a June report that, at that point, incoming revenue would cover just 78% of scheduled benefits from that fund. Without congressional action, those shortfalls would mean across-the-board reductions in benefits.

There is already a demographic 'run' on Social Security.

"The program's long-run outlook worsened significantly this year," it said. "The Social Security Administration (SSA) revised its fertility and immigration projections downward." The 75-year shortfall has risen to approximately $30 trillion - up from $26 trillion last year.

There is already a demographic "run" on Social Security. The Bipartisan Policy Center said "an aging population is a major contributor to the problem." The ratio of workers to beneficiaries has dropped from 5-to-1 in 1960 to 2.6-to-1 in 2025 and is projected to fall to 1.9-to-1 by 2075.

As the AARP report noted, some lawmakers propose lifting the payroll tax cap and taxing investment income for high earners to bring revenue as a share of GDP closer to historical levels, strengthening the program's finances without burdening lower- and middle-income workers.

The Social Security Disability Insurance Trust Fund is projected to remain solvent until 2100, the end of the Board of Trustees' 75-year projection period, but the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund, under current estimates, won't have enough to pay full benefits in 2032.

We are encouraged to delay our dream life, save more, work longer and maximize our retirement contributions. Still, the price of financial security should not be spending our 60s worrying about our 70s, 80s and 90s, and beyond. For millions of people, however, that worry is a daily reality.

Keep calm and carry on working, if you can, and saving for retirement.

Related: Should wealthier Americans forgo their Social Security benefits as a charitable gesture?

data.title: Studio McGee and The Oak Group Spotlight Development Partnership Behind First Full-Size Home Furnishings Flagship
data.description:
Studio McGee and The Oak Group Spotlight Development Partnership Behind First Full-Size Home Furnishings Flagship

Studio McGee and The Oak Group Spotlight Development Partnership Behind First Full-Size Home Furnishings Flagship

PR Newswire

SALT LAKE CITY, Nov. 19, 2026

Spanning more than 7,000 square feet, the flagship marks a major milestone for Studio McGee's growing home furnishings business, supported by The Oak Group's retail development expertise and proprietary SiteRise platform

SALT LAKE CITY, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Studio McGee, the acclaimed interior design firm and home furnishings brand known for its timeless, approachable aesthetic, and The Oak Group, a full-service retail development, design, and construction firm, today announced the success of their collaboration on Studio McGee's first full-size home furnishings flagship at Salt Lake City's historic Trolley Square.

The more than 7,000-square-foot store, which opened in September, marks a major milestone in Studio McGee's growing home furnishings business. Behind the flagship is a development partnership that brought together Studio McGee's distinctive design vision, The Oak Group's expertise in complex retail buildouts, and its proprietary SiteRise platform to coordinate the many moving parts involved in bringing the space to life.

Founded by Syd and Shea McGee in 2014, Studio McGee has grown from an interior design firm into a nationally recognized lifestyle brand, expanding its reach through McGee & Co., its home furnishings e-commerce business, and collaborations with leading retailers. The flagship represents a new chapter in that growth, giving customers a dedicated destination to explore furniture, décor, and home accessories while experiencing the brand's signature aesthetic firsthand.

Translating that vision into a physical retail environment required balancing intricate custom design elements with the practical demands of construction and development within a historic property. Studio McGee partnered with The Oak Group to execute the project, combining hands-on development and construction expertise with SiteRise, a platform designed to centralize project schedules, documentation, approvals, and stakeholder communication. Together, these capabilities helped the team maintain visibility, coordinate vendors, and manage key milestones throughout the buildout.

"Opening our first full-size flagship is an incredibly exciting moment for Studio McGee," said Shea McGee, Founder and Designer of Studio McGee. "We wanted to create a space where customers could experience our approach to design firsthand and feel inspired to bring that same beauty and intention into their own homes. The Oak Group understood what we were trying to achieve and helped translate that vision into a physical space. Having SiteRise as a central place for communication and project updates also made it easier to stay connected throughout the process. We're incredibly proud of what we've created together."

The flagship features a variety of thoughtful, custom design elements that reflect Studio McGee's signature balance of timeless style, comfort, and functionality. Highlights include intricate wood carvings crafted from scratch, decorative transom beams at interior room entrances, and a fully constructed entry vestibule designed to recreate the welcoming experience of stepping into a home. Together, these elements create an inviting retail environment where customers can discover and shop the brand's home furnishings collections.

For The Oak Group, the project presented the challenge of translating a highly recognizable design aesthetic into a functioning commercial space while navigating the complexities of Trolley Square's historic setting. From custom construction and vendor management to stakeholder coordination and the finer details of the customer experience, the team worked to preserve Studio McGee's creative vision throughout the development process.

"Studio McGee has built a brand where every detail matters, and that attention to detail carried through the entire project," said Kevin Porter, Director of Development at The Oak Group. "Our job was to bring the design to life while managing everything happening behind the scenes. Building in a historic location like Trolley Square came with its share of challenges, but we were able to step forward as a team and deliver a beautiful product that stayed true to Shea's original vision. It's a project we're incredibly proud to have been part of."

The flagship also serves as a real-world example of how technology can support increasingly complex retail development projects. Rather than relying on disconnected spreadsheets, email threads, and individual tracking systems, SiteRise provides teams with a centralized view of project information, helping improve visibility, communication, and decision-making from planning through opening.

"Retail development involves a lot of moving parts, and even small communication gaps can create significant challenges," said Dillon Okner, Founder of SiteRise and Founding Partner at The Oak Group. "We built SiteRise to give everyone involved a clearer picture of what's happening across a project, from timelines and approvals to outstanding decisions. The Studio McGee flagship is a great example of how that visibility can support the people doing the work, helping them stay focused on execution rather than chasing information."

The collaboration underscores the growing importance of combining development expertise, custom construction, and centralized technology as retail brands invest in physical spaces that reflect their identities and support their expansion.

For more information about Studio McGee and its flagship store, visit www.studio-mcgee.com.

To learn more about The Oak Group and SiteRise, visit www.theoakgroup.llc and www.siterise.app.

About The Oak Group

The Oak Group is a full-service retail development, design, and construction firm specializing in rapid, multi-site buildouts and renovations. The team supports brands at every stage of expansion—from real estate search and financial planning to design, vendor sourcing, and construction execution—helping ensure projects are delivered on time, on budget, and at scale. With experience supporting leading brands including Apple, Tesla, GAP, and Lilly Pulitzer, The Oak Group combines operational expertise with a hands-on approach to streamline complex development processes. The company is also the force behind SiteRise, its platform designed to bring greater visibility and coordination to multi-site growth.

To learn more, visit www.theoakgroup.llc or follow The Oak Group on LinkedIn.

About SiteRise

SiteRise, from The Oak Group, is a platform built to help brands plan, open, and scale physical locations with greater speed and control. It brings site selection, deal tracking, and development workflows into one place—giving real estate, legal, design, and construction teams a shared system to collaborate and execute more efficiently. By integrating with existing tools and centralizing critical data, SiteRise serves as a single source of truth for multi-site growth.

To learn more, visit www.siterise.app and follow SiteRise on LinkedIn and Instagram.

About Studio McGee

Studio McGee is an interior design brand created in 2014 by husband-and-wife team, Syd and Shea McGee. Studio McGee's journey started on social media, quickly garnering the attention of a design-loving community through a steady stream of inspirational projects and consistent design tips. With a loyal social following, the design business experienced rapid growth, paving the way for the launch of their e-commerce brand, McGee & Co., along with a lineup of licensing partnerships and marketing opportunities that amplified Studio McGee's design voice. Today, Studio McGee continues to be creatively led by co-founder and chief creative officer, Shea McGee, and is regarded as one of the leading innovators in the interior design industry with a 'sophisticated but not stuffy' approach, while maintaining a consistent focus on empowering others to "Make Life Beautiful" by enhancing their daily lives through good design. For more information about Studio McGee, please visit studio-mcgee.com.

Bagel-Robotics-1, an open-weight model for autonomous robotics, outperforms OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and other models on shared benchmark tests.

TORONTO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Bagel Labs today announced Bagel-Robotics-1, an open-weight model ranked No. 3 worldwide among robot-control models on the RoboDojo benchmark, a global measure of progress in autonomous robotics that industry leaders like Anthropic use to evaluate their models.

RoboDojo tests whether an AI model can control a robot precisely, remember earlier steps, adapt to unfamiliar situations and complete tasks with multiple steps. Bagel-Robotics-1 scored higher than the GPT-6 Astra results published by the RoboDojo team in each of those areas.

Bagel-Robotics-1 is the highest-ranked entry from a North American company on RoboDojo's main leaderboard.

The release is part of Bagel Labs' broader research into general purpose robot-control models, with the goal of building capable autonomous robotics systems, including robotic arms and mobile robots, using smaller models.

data.title: Cumberland EMC and Base Power Launch Residential Battery Program to Bring Affordable Whole-Home Backup to Tennessee
data.description:
Cumberland EMC and Base Power Launch Residential Battery Program to Bring Affordable Whole-Home Backup to Tennessee

The 30-megawatt program is Base’s first partnership in Tennessee and TVA territory. The program offers members automatic home backup for a fraction of the cost of traditional options.

Cumberland Electric Membership Corporation (Cumberland EMC) and Base Power today announced a partnership to deploy 30 megawatts (MW) of residential battery storage across the cooperative’s service territory. The program will create a networked fleet that Cumberland EMC can dispatch to reduce demand at system peaks.

Base handles installation and maintenance of every battery, while the cooperative decides when the fleet charges and discharges. For Cumberland EMC, that means new local capacity added quickly and affordably, to cut wholesale power costs and generate savings for members.

The program comes on the heels of Winter Storm Fern, which left hundreds of thousands of Tennesseans without power earlier this year. It brings to Cumberland EMC an outage protection solution that already serves over 35,000 members and has recently expanded to Illinois and Georgia.

Cumberland EMC members can get a Base battery for $695 upfront plus $19 a month. That’s 95% less upfront than a traditional standby generator, which typically costs $13,000 or more. The Base Core battery can back up a home for up to 36 hours and, if needed, even longer using its portable generator charge port. Members pay only for the energy their home uses, at their regular Cumberland EMC rates.

“Cumberland EMC exists to deliver safe, affordable and reliable power the cooperative way. This program gives our members an affordable path to home backup power and gives the cooperative a smarter way to manage peak demand. We’re proud to be the first in the Tennessee Valley to offer it,” said Chris Davis, President and CEO of Cumberland EMC.

“Base is excited to partner with Cumberland EMC, our first partnership in Tennessee and TVA territory,” said Zach Dell, co-founder and CEO of Base Power. “This program gives families affordable home backup while also helping the cooperative build a stronger grid. We’re proud to bring Base to Tennessee as we continue to expand across the country and help utility partners like Cumberland EMC lead in delivering more affordable, reliable power.”

Cumberland EMC joins a growing list of Base’s utility partners, including Central Georgia EMC, Austin Energy, El Paso Electric, CoServ, Farmers Electric Cooperative, and Guadalupe Valley Electric Cooperative.

Installations are expected to begin in early 2027. Interested members can join the waitlist at www.basepowercompany.com.

For more on Base Power’s utility partnerships, visit www.basepowercompany.com/utilities.

About Base Power

Founded in 2023 and headquartered in Austin, Texas, Base Power is an energy company building a grid for the future. The company's mission is to advance human prosperity through energy abundance, delivering reliable and affordable power for all.

About Cumberland EMC

Cumberland Electric Membership Corporation is Tennessee’s third-largest distribution cooperative, serving more than 118,000 members across Cheatham, Montgomery, Robertson, Stewart, and Sumner counties with safe, affordable, and reliable services.

Her 16-Page Booklet Sold More Than Two Million Copies. Now Paulette Ensign Will Teach Five Ways to Turn Expertise into Income

Her 16-Page Booklet Sold More Than Two Million Copies. Now Paulette Ensign Will Teach Five Ways to Turn Expertise into Income

PR Newswire

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 19, 2026

January 12 live workshop helps participants explore what they could publish, sell, license, or secure sponsorship for using knowledge they already have.

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Paulette Ensign sold more than two million copies of a 16-page booklet called 110 Ideas for Organizing Your Business Life. She expanded its reach through bulk sales, licensing, and distribution partnerships. On Tuesday, January 12, 2027, she'll help others apply those lessons to a topic they know well in The TIPS Method Sampler Live Workshop.

The 90-minute Zoom workshop is designed for authors, speakers, coaches, consultants, nonprofit leaders, and other professionals with specialized knowledge. Participants will bring one topic and explore five ways to develop and distribute it:

  • Create a practical how-to tips publication
  • Publish and sell a book on Amazon
  • Sell publications in bulk
  • License content
  • Develop a publication with private donor sponsorship

Each participant will leave with a Personal Possibilities Map to help identify which options are worth pursuing before investing time and money in product development. The workshop includes a live Q&A with Ensign.

"My goal is to help participants recognize possibilities they may never have considered," said Ensign, founder of Tips Products International.

Workshop registration

The workshop runs from 1 to 2:30 p.m. ET (10 to 11:30 a.m. PT). The $300 registration fee includes the live workshop, access to The TIPS Method Sampler course, and a replay recording. Participants have one year from the workshop date to apply the full $300 registration fee toward any course in Ensign's Uniquely Monetize Your Knowledge suite.

Registration closes Monday, January 11, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. ET. Register for the workshop.

data.title: Origin Investments/Mill Creek Residential Announce Modera Paradise Valley II in Phoenix
data.description:
Origin Investments/Mill Creek Residential Announce Modera Paradise Valley II in Phoenix

Origin Investments/Mill Creek Residential Announce Modera Paradise Valley II in Phoenix

PR Newswire

CHICAGO, Nov. 19, 2026

Origin Launches $52.7 Million Single Asset QOZ Investment Opportunity Intersecting QOZ 2.0 Benefits and the QOZ 1.0 Map

CHICAGO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Origin Investments, a leading private real estate firm, and Mill Creek Residential, a national investment and rental housing company, have announced plans for Modera Paradise Valley II, a 380-unit Class A multifamily community that is within the Paradise Valley Mall redevelopment area and includes 500,000 square feet of walkable retail space.

Origin will fund the project as a single-asset Qualified Opportunity Zone (QOZ) investment and raise $52.7 million in equity. The offering will accept capital beginning January 1, 2027, when the "OZ 2.0" tax benefits created by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act take effect. The benefits of investing capital gains in a Qualified Opportunity Fund include a rolling five-year deferral of federal capital gains tax, a 10% basis step-up after five years, and tax-free appreciation after a 10-year hold. 

The Modera Paradise Valley II site sits in one of Phoenix's original Opportunity Zones, designated in 2018. Treasury guidance issued this year allows new investment into original-zone projects after 2026 as long as the project has a qualifying working capital plan in place and meets certain other qualified opportunity zone business requirements. Modera Paradise Valley II intends to fulfill those requirements.

"Modera Paradise Valley II is an OZ offering that features the investment benefits of 2.0 while developing a 1.0 location," said Michael Episcope, Co-CEO, Origin Investments. "We believe the stars are finally aligning in the multifamily sector to create meaningful upside for investors, and we believe this location is one of the best in the country."

Those factors, according to Episcope, include partnering with an experienced developer and general contractor like Mill Creek Residential, completing Modera Paradise Valley II at a strong, competitive cost basis with conservative rent positioning, and delivering the project at a time when we expect demand may outpace supply. 

The benefits of an investment in the project include:

  • Trophy Location—Positioned within the Paradise Valley Mall redevelopment, the property is to sit alongside premium retail anchors including Life Time Fitness and Whole Foods. Including those anchors, the site is walkable to approximately 500,000 square feet of retail and entertainment options.

  • Below Market Basis—Origin and MCR expect to deliver the new community at approximately $400K per unit, well below recent comparable trades in the immediate area. The parcel is already zoned for multifamily by-right, so no rezoning or entitlement process remains. Rents are underwritten conservatively, leaving room for upside if performance tracks comparable properties in the area.

  • Experienced Partnership—Mill Creek Residential will serve as both developer and general contractor. With over 30 years of experience and more than 275,000 rental homes delivered, this will be their 10th Phoenix project and third with Origin, which Origin believes supports its confidence in on-budget delivery.

  • Opportunity Zone 2.0 Benefits—An investment funded after January 1, 2027, provides the following benefits: Federal tax on the original capital gain is deferred for five years; after a 5-year hold, the basis in the deferred gain steps up by 10%; and after a 10-year hold, investors can step up the basis in their investment to its fair market value, permanently excluding appreciation and depreciation recapture from federal taxes.

The minimum contribution for an investment in this opportunity zone investment is $50,000. Origin is targeting a net equity multiple ranging from 2.0 to 2.3x and a net IRR of 9-11% based on a holding period of 10 years. These targets are not guarantees, and actual performance may differ. 

Modera Paradise Valley II, located at 4510 E Cactus Road on a 4.94-acre parcel, is planned as a 380-unit, Class A wrap development that will mirror the quality standards established at Mill Creek's Modera branded communities across the country. The development will be comprised of one-, two-, and three-bedroom apartment homes. 

In keeping with MCR's Modera brand, Modera Paradise Valley II will feature top-of-market, hospitality-inspired amenities, including a resort-style pool, outdoor kitchen, poolside cabanas, lounge seating, and outdoor grilling and entertainment areas with fire features. That caliber of amenities will extend to the resident clubhouse and include an entertainment lounge, modern dining and bar space, and a membership-quality fitness center. Additional offerings include high-end coworking spaces, and private conference rooms. 

Apartment home interiors will include a variety of deluxe features, including stainless steel appliances, quartz countertops, tile backsplashes, luxury vinyl-plank flooring, premium cabinetry, kitchen islands, undermount sinks, under-cabinet lighting, full-size washers and dryers, private patios or balconies, roller shades and a variety of smart home features, including smart thermostats and keyless entry. Bathrooms are planned to feature double vanities, tile tub and shower surrounds and backlit LED mirrors. 

Construction of Modera Paradise Valley II could begin as early as Spring 2027. Completion would occur approximately 24 months later. 

The Modera Paradise Valley II site is within a coveted submarket in the Phoenix MSA. It is situated at the convergence of Cactus Rd. and Tatum Blvd. which provides quality access to Loop 101 and Route 51. This location connects residents to the greater Phoenix region. The Town of Paradise Valley, located 1.3 miles south, has an average household income of $408K and an average home value of $5M.

Paradise Valley is an affluent enclave between Phoenix and Scottsdale, known for luxury resorts, high-end retail, and some of the metro's strongest household-income demographics. More than 185,000 jobs are located within seven miles, with major employment concentrations in healthcare and financial services. Additionally, the affordability rating in a three-mile radius surrounding the site is 24. Modera Paradise Valley II is well positioned and aligned with the demographics for the area.

"Modera Paradise Valley II has the critical attributes that we believe are necessary to be a successful multifamily investment even before it derives any additional investor benefits from being in an opportunity zone," said Jacob Sojka, Vice President, Origin Investments. "We're very excited about adding this to our portfolio of properties in Arizona and across the West and Southwestern U.S."

The release of plans for Modera Paradise Valley II follows the recent announcement that Origin and Mill Creek Residential are partnering on Modera Old Town, a 190-unit OZ development in Old Town Scottsdale.

Since 2018, Origin has announced more than 20 opportunity zone investments with plans to develop more than 5,000 units. Similarly, MCR has made 12 opportunity zone investments to develop approximately 3,800 units. Origin is a top 2% national qualified opportunity zone (QOZ) fund manager1 based on capital raised according to Novogradac, a national certified public accounting (CPA) and consulting firm that specializes in real estate, community development, and tax incentives.

  1. Origin was ranked 11th out of 993 Qualified Opportunity Zone fund managers in terms of the amount of equity raised, according to the Novogradac Opportunity Zones Investment Report. As of 6/30/25. 

About Mill Creek Residential 

Mill Creek Residential is a national investment and rental housing company focused on developing, constructing, and operating multifamily and built-to-rent communities in targeted markets nationwide. Headquartered in Boca Raton, Florida, the company operates across the United States through a seasoned team of professionals, with a presence in many of the nation's most desirable markets, including Seattle, Portland, the San Francisco Bay Area, Sacramento, Southern California, Salt Lake City, Phoenix, Denver, Dallas, Austin, Houston, South Florida, Tampa, Orlando, Atlanta, Nashville, Charlotte, Raleigh, Washington, D.C., New Jersey, New York, and Boston. As of June 30, 2026, the company's portfolio is comprised of 153 communities representing nearly 43,000 rental homes operating or under construction. Visit MillCreekPlaces.com for more information. 

About Origin Investments 

Founded in 2007, Origin Investments is a private real estate manager that helps high-net-worth investors, family offices and registered investment advisors grow and preserve wealth by providing tax-efficient real estate solutions through private funds. We build, buy and finance multifamily real estate projects in fast-growing markets throughout the U.S. In 2023, we founded affiliate firm Origin Credit Advisers, an SEC-registered investment adviser that provides yield-focused multifamily debt investments. Registration with the SEC does not imply a certain level of skill or training and does not constitute an endorsement, approval, or sponsorship by the SEC. Through our Origin Exchange platform, introduced in 2024, investors can complete a 1031 exchange of their properties for professionally managed, institutional-quality assets. To learn more, visit www.origininvestments.com.

data.title: Stock Futures Rise Ahead of Anthropic Trading Debut — Update
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

Nasdaq futures led a rally in U.S. stocks premarket, after Anthropic's pricing of its hotly anticipated listing lifted confidence around the artificial-intelligence trade.

The expectation-beating IPO pricing of the company behind the Claude chatbot helped investor focus shift away from the AI jitters that have weighed on stocks so far this week. However, sentiment was tempered by hawkish Federal Reserve meeting minutes Wednesday that added to fears of extended policy tightening.

Nasdaq futures jumped 2% as chip makers and cloud-computing stocks rallied premarket. Anthropic sold more shares at a higher price than anticipated, implying a value of around $1.5 trillion for the company. S&P 500 futures were also in the green--up 1.2%--as the index looks to turn the tide on a fifth-straight day of losses. Contracts tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.6%. The index has fallen by more than 1% for three days in a row.

Equities were mixed across Asia, where the tech-dominated Nikkei Stock Average in Japan and South Korea's Kospi closed in the green. Stock indexes in Hong Kong and Shanghai fell, however. In Europe, major indexes were mixed as the continent-wide Stoxx 600 slipped 0.1%.

Treasury yields ticked higher after falling in Asian trade, as investors respond to a hawkish readout from the Fed's October meeting. Near-term rate-sensitive two-year yields rose above 4.800%, while 10-year yields nudged back toward 5.100%. Thirty-year yields hovered around 5.440%.

Oil prices rose, picking up from falls Wednesday after U.S. crude oil inventories rose for a second consecutive week. The benchmark Brent crude contract rose 1% to trade around $93 a barrel, while the West Texas Intermediate contract nudged up 0.9% to trade around $84 a barrel.

The dollar fell slightly, but remained close to its highest level against a basket of global currencies since January 2025. Copper prices steadied after falling sharply in the last session but gold extended losses, trading close to $3,700 a troy ounce. Bitcoin rallied after recent declines, adding over 2% to trade around $63,750.

Anthropic's trading debut will be in focus for the day ahead. Investors will also watch for readouts from the trilateral meeting between President Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen.
